text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Diagnosis: a structured headache history, a red-flag screen (SNNOOP10) at every visit, a 14-day diary of headache days, attack features, triggers and every dose of acute medicine, and ICHD-3 criteria; MRI of the brain with and without contrast because the headaches have become more frequent over the past year, are strongly right-sided, and come with long-standing unequal pupils and a very poor right eye; treponemal and nontreponemal syphilis serology because of past gonorrhea, unequal pupils and poor vision
  • Neurology (headache medicine) consultation to confirm the diagnosis and advise on withdrawal of the overused tablets and on preventive treatment
  • Medication overuse at intake: explain how frequent combination tablets can keep headaches going; count every tablet and acute-medicine day in the diary; take no more than now and never more than four combination tablets a day until the consultation; no new sedatives or sleeping tablets
  • Comprehensive eye examination for high myopia: refraction, pupils, pressure, a dilated fundus examination for myopic degeneration, retinal breaks and lattice, and macular OCT; correction of the large difference between the eyes; the warning signs of retinal detachment and an Amsler grid; dilated examination every year
  • Withdrawal: stop ibuprofen and replace as-needed butalbital combination tablets with a scheduled three-week taper (twice a day, then once a day, then every other day), because barbiturates are tapered rather than stopped abruptly; warn about rebound headache in the first one to two weeks and about the rare risk of withdrawal seizures; start prevention at the same time
  • Acute treatment after withdrawal: naproxen with metoclopramide early in an attack, no more than two days a week; sumatriptan added once the taper is complete, with no more than eight triptan days a month; no butalbital, opioids or combination products with caffeine
  • Preventive treatment for chronic migraine: galcanezumab 240 mg loading dose, then 120 mg monthly, judged at three months (at least half as many monthly migraine days); topiramate not chosen because of its effects on word-finding and concentration and its rare acute myopia with angle-closure glaucoma, a poor fit for a writer with high myopia; erenumab not chosen because of his constipation; onabotulinumtoxinA, every 12 weeks, as the next option or an addition
  • Sleep: cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia through the clinic's behavioral sleep program, a fixed rising time, a wind-down hour, and no sedative sleeping tablets
  • Mood: PHQ-9 and GAD-7 at intake and at about two to three months, with direct questions about hopelessness and self-harm at each visit; a safety assessment if a score or answer calls for one
  • Reading, writing and walking: good light, large print and an enlarged screen, breaks every 30 minutes, voice dictation for long passages, sunglasses and a brimmed hat for glare, and his daily walks kept as a protected part of the plan

resource.title: Friedrich Nietzsche synthetic care plan
resource.description: Frequent headache with medicine overuse in a writer with very poor eyesight: a 36-year-old former professor who left his post for ill health, newly arrived in a mountain village for the summer, has headaches on about 20 days a month and takes a butalbital combination on most of them. The episode covers a structured headache history and the SNNOOP10 red-flag screen, and when imaging is justified (a strongly one-sided pattern, a change in frequency, long-standing unequal pupils and a poor eye); MRI of the brain with and without contrast; treponemal and nontreponemal syphilis serology when the history calls for it; ICHD-3 criteria for chronic migraine and medication overuse headache from a two-week diary; withdrawal of overused medicine, with a slow taper of the barbiturate rather than abrupt withdrawal, under the 1875 European Academy of Neurology guideline; preventive treatment for chronic migraine under the 1876 American Headache Society consensus, its 1879 CGRP position statement and the 1877 European Headache Federation guideline, choosing a CGRP monoclonal antibody over topiramate (cognitive effects and acute myopia with angle closure) and onabotulinumtoxinA; limits on acute medicine afterwards; high and pathologic myopia under the American Academy of Ophthalmology Preferred Practice Patterns, including a dilated fundus examination, correction of large anisometropia with contact lenses, and the warning signs of retinal detachment; insomnia treated without sedatives; mood screening; and protecting his reading, writing and long walks.
